# Model card: Purchase Intent Engine (full data, K = 5)

*Generated by `scripts/08_model_cards.py` on 16 November 2026 from `results/tables`. Do not edit by hand.*

## Model
- **Engine model:** GRU (sequence) (deep learning, K. Ray), chosen as the fastest of the models statistically tied for the best PR-AUC at K = 5 (Random forest, GRU (sequence); paired bootstrap, Holm-corrected, α = 0.05).
- **Input:** the first 5 events (views and add-to-carts) of a visit: time, product, category, brand, price.
- **Output:** a score in [0, 1], a buyer / non-buyer decision at a threshold tuned on the validation weeks (F1), an intent level (high, warm, browsing) and a suggested action. At its threshold the engine model reaches 0.39 precision and 0.41 recall on the test weeks.
- **Serving:** `src/serving/predictor.py` (Python), `src/api/app.py` (REST, `POST /score`), dashboard Live scoring page. The same feature code is used in training and serving.

## Intended use
- Rank live visits by purchase intent to decide *who should not get a discount* (high intent buys anyway) and who gets a nudge. See the Campaign planner page for the money involved.
- **Out of scope:** decisions about individuals with legal or similarly significant effects, credit, pricing per person, or any use outside the shop's own visitors. The score is not a calibrated probability.

## Training data
- REES46 multi-category shop, 2019-Oct to 2020-Apr, 10% random sample of whole visits (8,871,684 visits, 40,111,556 events). See the data card.
- Chronological split by visit start: train 2019-10-01 → 2020-03-01 (1,315,346 visits), validation → 2020-04-04 (284,513), test 2020-04-04 → 2020-04-30 (295,645, 10.2% buy).

## Performance (test weeks)
PR-AUC mean ± std over 3 seeds; 95 % CI from a bootstrap of the primary seed; lift = PR-AUC / buyer rate (random = 1×). Precision and recall at each model's tuned threshold.

| Model | Team | PR-AUC | 95% CI | Lift | Precision | Recall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Random forest | machine learning, M. Kara | 0.337 ± 0.000 | 0.332–0.343 | 3.3× | 0.39 | 0.41 |
| GRU (sequence) **(engine)** | deep learning, K. Ray | 0.336 ± 0.001 | 0.330–0.341 | 3.3× | 0.39 | 0.41 |
| LightGBM | machine learning, M. Kara | 0.333 ± 0.000 | 0.327–0.339 | 3.3× | 0.39 | 0.41 |
| MLP | deep learning, K. Ray | 0.333 ± 0.000 | 0.327–0.339 | 3.3× | 0.38 | 0.42 |
| TabNet | deep learning, K. Ray | 0.326 ± 0.002 | 0.319–0.330 | 3.2× | 0.37 | 0.43 |
| Logistic regression | machine learning, M. Kara | 0.325 ± 0.000 | 0.320–0.331 | 3.2× | 0.38 | 0.43 |
| Rule baseline | machine learning, M. Kara | 0.214 | 0.211–0.218 | 2.1× | 0.35 | 0.45 |

## Explanations
- Most influential features across models (share of attribution): price_std (17%), view_count (13%), main_category (10%), has_cart (8%), hour_of_day (7%).
- Cart signals are the top feature group for 13/15 model × K combinations.
- LightGBM per-visit explanations (TreeSHAP) are returned by the API with `explain: true`.

## Monitoring (validation and test weeks)
- Weekly PR-AUC of the engine model: 0.254–0.435 over 11 weeks; lift 3.2×–3.9×. Weekly accuracy follows the weekly buyer rate.
- Input drift (PSI vs training): major in no feature; moderate in no feature.
- Alert rule: weekly 95 % CI below the test PR-AUC for two weeks, or any PSI > 0.25.

## Limitations
- 55% of test buyers (16,454 of 30,046) show no buying signal in their first clicks and are missed by every model.
- Scores rank visits but are not calibrated probabilities (models were trained with class balancing).
- One shop, Oct 2019 – Apr 2020: patterns may differ in other shops, seasons or after site changes.
- REES46 changed its category tree in December 2019; labels were mapped back to the Oct/Nov tree (data card). Products with no category stay `unknown`.
- The campaign planner's money figures depend on an assumed offer effect; measure it with an A/B test.

## Ethical considerations
- Inputs are behavioural events of an anonymous visit; no names, contact details or demographics are used. `user_id` is not a model input.
- Withholding a discount from high-intent visitors changes what different visitors are offered; the shop should make sure offers stay within its pricing and consumer-protection rules.

## Maintenance
- Retrain monthly on a rolling window (`scripts/01`–`03`), rerun benchmarks, monitoring and these cards (`scripts/05`, `07`, `08`).
- Owners: machine-learning models M. Kara; deep-learning models K. Ray.
